title: The Editors’ Table
paragraphs: At a table covered with draft pages, a group of young editors discussed their next publication. Each person had brought a different account. Rather than rank the experiences from best to worst, they decided to explore the connections among them and preserve the details that mattered.

Several records provided a starting point for the discussion. The shocked visitor could not utter a single word. Her emphatic refusal left no doubt that she would not agree. Repeated interruptions can exasperate even a patient teacher. Seeing innocent people blamed would infuriate the fair-minded judge.

Other records complicated that first impression and encouraged a closer reading. It is cruel to mock a classmate for making a mistake. Do not belittle her achievement just because the task seemed easy to you. The coach told spectators not to jeer at the visiting players. The ranger had to admonish visitors who fed the wild animals.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

targets.definition: to make fun of someone in an unkind way
to make someone or something seem less important
to shout rude remarks or laugh scornfully at someone
to warn or correct someone firmly
